How to use the matching information

Gujarat's craft geography becomes easier to understand when each tradition is connected with its principal production method, artisan community and geographical centre. The table below brings these relationships together.

The community column identifies the principal traditional association rather than claiming exclusive ownership of a craft. Similarly, the district column gives a major cultural or production centre; it does not, by itself, define the precise legal geographical boundaries of a registered GI.

Craft–community–district–GI table

Craft or GI productTraditional communityDistrict or centreGI registration
Patan PatolaSalvi weaversPatan2013
Rajkot PatolaIkat weaversRajkot2018
Jamnagari BandhaniKhatri dyersJamnagar2016
Kutch Bandhani of GujaratKhatri dyersKutch: Bhuj, Mandvi2024
Kutch Ajrakh Print of GujaratKhatri printersKutch: Ajrakhpur, Dhamadka2024
Tangaliya ShawlDangasia weaversSurendranagar: Wadhwan region2009
Kutch Rogan CraftKhatri paintersKutch: Nirona2024
Banni embroideryJat, Mutwa, Meghwal and other groupsBanni region, KutchKutch Embroidery GI: 2008
Rabari embroideryRabari womenKutch; also wider GujaratKutch forms: GI of 2008
Ahir embroideryAhir womenKutchKutch Embroidery GI: 2008
Sankheda FurnitureKharadi and Suthar woodworkersChhota Udepur: Sankheda2008
Saurashtra Moti BharatkamSeveral groups, including Kathi, Kanbi and AhirSaurashtra; Bhavnagar association2026
Mata ni PachediDevipujak or Vaghri; Chitara paintersAhmedabad2023

All the explicitly named GI products in this table were recorded as registered in the official 31 October 2026 GI snapshot. The years shown are registration certificate years, not application-filing years. For Saurashtra Moti Bharatkam, the GI record contains a registration certificate document dated 28 March 2026.

The entries for Banni, Rabari and Ahir embroidery are different: they identify regional or community styles, while Kutch Embroidery is the relevant broadly named GI registered in 2008. This does not mean that every form of Rabari embroidery from every part of Gujarat automatically satisfies that GI's registered specifications.

Remember the major geographical clusters

Kutch has the greatest concentration of the listed textile-decoration traditions. It includes Bandhani, Ajrakh, Rogan and several distinct embroidery styles. Within Kutch, the exact locality provides a more precise identification: Ajrakhpur and Dhamadka for Ajrakh, Nirona for Rogan, and Banni for a group of embroidery traditions.

Patan is the primary centre of traditional double-ikat Patola. Rajkot is associated with its distinct Patola tradition. Jamnagar is a major Bandhani centre.

Surendranagar is associated with Tangaliya weaving, while Saurashtra more broadly includes beadwork traditions associated with several communities and districts. Chhota Udepur is associated with Sankheda furniture, and Ahmedabad with Mata-ni-Pachedi.

High-value distinctions in matching and statement questions

Community and region are not interchangeable

The terms Salvi, Khatri, Dangasia, Rabari, Ahir and Devipujak refer to artisan or social communities in the relevant craft context. The terms Kutch, Saurashtra and Banni refer to geographical areas. Banni is located within Kutch; Saurashtra is a wider region containing several districts.

One community may practise several crafts

Khatri artisans are associated with Bandhani, Ajrakh and Rogan. A statement identifying a craft merely by the Khatri community is therefore incomplete. The material, technique and production centre must also be considered.

One district may contain several craft centres

Kutch includes Nirona, Ajrakhpur, Dhamadka, Bhuj and Mandvi. Therefore, the district Kutch alone cannot distinguish Rogan from Ajrakh or Bandhani. More precise place names and craft methods resolve the ambiguity.

A craft tradition is not necessarily a separate GI

GI registration applies to a specific registered geographical product name. The existence of the GI Kutch Embroidery does not establish separate GI registrations under the individual names Banni embroidery, Rabari embroidery and Ahir embroidery.

Historical and present district names can differ

Sankheda may appear under Vadodara in older books and records, but its current administrative district is Chhota Udepur. The date and context of a district reference therefore matter.

Recognition clues for rapid revision

  • Both warp and weft yarns resist-dyed: Patan Patola.
  • Small tied portions of cloth creating dots: Bandhani.
  • Repeated patterns produced with wooden blocks: Ajrakh.
  • Castor-oil-based painting in Nirona: Rogan.
  • Raised daana dots woven into cloth: Tangaliya.
  • Needlework and mirror traditions of Kutch communities: Banni, Rabari and Ahir embroidery.
  • Lacquered and painted wooden cradles or swings: Sankheda furniture.
  • Glass-bead torans and decorative household objects: Saurashtra Moti Bharatkam.
  • Devipujak ritual cloth associated with Mother Goddess worship: Mata-ni-Pachedi.

Prelims focus

  • Salvi — Patan — Patola; Dangasia — Surendranagar — Tangaliya.
  • Khatri — Ajrakhpur and Dhamadka — Ajrakh; Khatri — Nirona — Rogan.
  • Devipujak or Vaghri — Ahmedabad — Mata-ni-Pachedi.
  • Kharadi — Sankheda — Chhota Udepur district.
  • Banni is a Kutch region; Rabari and Ahir are community identities.
  • GI snapshot cutoff: 31 October 2026; Saurashtra Moti Bharatkam is registered with a 2026 certificate document.
  • Trap: Do not confuse the filing date displayed in a GI list with the certificate date.

[Sources: GCERT, Social Science, Standard 10, Chapter 2, sections on traditional handloom, Bandhani, embroidery, beadwork and woodworking; NCERT, Living Craft Traditions of India, Class 11, Chapter 1, Crafts Heritage, printed pp. 9–12; Gujarat Tourism, Patola, Bandhani, Tangaliya, Nirona and Sankheda Furniture craft and destination documentation, consulted 23 November 2026; Khamir, Ajrakh Blockprint, Bandhani, Rogan Painting and Embroidery, consulted 23 November 2026; Sahapedia, Kalamkari of Gujarat: Mata ni Pachhedi, consulted 23 November 2026; Intellectual Property India, Details of GI Applications Registered as on 31 October 2026, Gujarat entries 142–168, and GI Registry application records 100, 103, 127, 221, 232, 380, 694, 718, 756, 1050 and 1280, consulted 23 November 2026.]
